findings.title: README digest check is a weak substring match
findings.message: The checker hashes README text via substring search `app['archive_sha256'] in README.md`. This only proves the digest appears somewhere in the README, not that it is in the right row, so swapped or misattributed digests would pass. The checker is the stated control for checksum consistency.
findings.suggestion: Parse the README table rows and compare each app name to its digest, instead of searching for the digest anywhere in the file.
findings.evidence: require(all(a['visual_result'] == ('held-dark-contrast' if a['id'] == 'shell' else 'pass') for a in native['apps']), 'visual outcome mismatch')

findings.title: Missing asset file crashes with unhandled exception
findings.message: The tar evidence reader enforces safe names but `--assets` paths and `args.packet` are joined without checks, and member reads via `stream.read()` load up to 16MB each into memory. The more significant gap: a missing asset raises FileNotFoundError, not a clear validation error, so the tool crashes instead of reporting a failed check.
findings.suggestion: Check `(args.assets / name).is_file()` with require() before hashing, so a missing archive yields a clear failure message.
findings.evidence: require(digest(args.assets / name) == expected_hash, 'actual archive mismatch: ' + name)
